title: A visitor who declines analytics cookies still has their Create a Space steps and QR scans sent to Google Analytics

source.ref: Mega pass 2026-11-19 (unknown-unknowns audit: consent and third parties)

detail: Mega pass 2026-11-19. lib/analytics/track.ts mirrors an event to the GA4 Measurement Protocol and checks consent only when there is a signed-in actor. Two request-backed callers send events with no actor: the signed-out Create a Space builder's nine funnel steps (app/api/create-space/signal/route.ts) and qr.scanned for an anonymous scanner (app/q/[slug]/route.ts, which also skipped the browser's decline cookie for a signed-in scanner). So a visitor who declined analytics still had those events sent to Google, each under a made-up client id that counts as a new GA user. lead.captured and account.created already asked requestGoogleAllowed() (lib/analytics/server-google-policy.ts). Fix: both routes ask it and pass mirrorGa, so the first-party count always lands and Google gets a copy only with consent. Webhook and cron mirrors with no request are unchanged (LIVE-2275).

verify.note: Fails on main: neither route asks the browser's consent. Passes when both pass mirrorGa from requestGoogleAllowed().
